summary: pmcro-reflector's Complete-ReflectAndSeed.ps1 computes its default -QueueRoot as Join-Path (Split-Path (Split-Path $PmcroRoot -Parent) -Parent) '.pmcro\queue' -- this only lands correctly when -PmcroRoot is passed as the exact relative form '.\.pmcro' from the repo root. When -PmcroRoot is passed as an absolute path (e.g. 'P:\ProjectName\.pmcro', needed because callers' working directories vary across tool invocations), the double Split-Path -Parent walks up two levels from the drive root instead of from the repo root, and the queue item silently gets written outside the repo entirely (observed: written to 'P:\.pmcro\queue\' -- an unrelated, pre-existing directory at the drive root -- instead of the repo's '.pmcro\queue\'). No error or warning is raised; the script reports next_seed_enqueued: true and status: ok even though the file landed in the wrong place. Fix: derive QueueRoot from the resolved trail directory's own ancestry (e.g. walk up from $trailDir, which is already known-correct, rather than re-deriving from $PmcroRoot with parent-count arithmetic that assumes a specific relative path shape), or require -QueueRoot to be supplied explicitly whenever -PmcroRoot is absolute. Add a script or Pester-style check that calls Complete-ReflectAndSeed.ps1 with an absolute -PmcroRoot and asserts the queue item lands under that same root's queue/ folder. Discovered while hand-running trail 0aa1c59d-6941-4692-9d40-4b893eb9fe5d's reflect-and-seed step; the misplaced file was found and manually relocated to the correct .pmcro/queue/ during that session.
